content.content:
Applied at check time by reading the born node's recorded relations against the invocation that produced it; each criterion is decided over those two records only.
1. License: no element of the dependent contradicts a prerequisite named in depends_on. Fail on any contradicting element — name the element and the parent it contradicts.
2. Total: every id given to the linkage flag in the invocation appears in the born node's evaluates. Fail on any given id absent from evaluates — name the id and the invocation.
3. Faithful: every id in the born node's evaluates was given to the linkage flag in that invocation. Fail on any id present that the caller did not give — name the id, and where it can be traced, where it came from (a placement id, the summary, elsewhere).
4. Routed: no id given to the linkage flag appears in the born node's depends_on, and the born node's depends_on names exactly the ids given to the placement flag. Fail on any linkage-named id landing in depends_on — name the id.
5. Repetition: an id given to the linkage flag more than once in one invocation is still recorded in evaluates, and the repetition admits no id that was not given. Fail on an id given twice and absent from evaluates, or on an id present only because of the repetition — name the id.
6. Not displaced: an id given to both the linkage flag and the placement flag is recorded in evaluates and in depends_on; neither spelling drops it from the other relation. Fail on a shared id missing from either relation — name the id.
7. Silent when unnamed: an invocation that does not name the linkage flag produces a node with no evaluates edge — the key is absent, and an empty array does not stand in for its absence. Fail on an evaluates key in a node born without the flag.
8. Order- and repetition-neutral: two invocations whose linkage-flag id lists differ only in order and repetition produce nodes whose evaluates name the same set of ids. Fail on an id named in one set and not the other — name the id.
content.rationale: The dependent's one commitment is a linkage: which ids the birth records in the new node's evaluates. Birth is a requirement sentence, so the strongest row is structured against a structured child — the matrix default cell, which is the gate form; the flag's surface and the skeleton's fixed fields are inline prose, the natural-to-structured cell, also the gate form (default cell used — flagged for a matrix entry). The linkage criteria narrow the license check to the single relation the child adds: totality, no accretion, correct relation, repetition, shared ids, silence when unnamed and order-neutrality. The kind split, the guard over unknown ids and the node's own content stay with the decisions that own them, and the check reads only recorded relations against the invocation, so it survives a rewording that decides the same linkage.
